head_commit.message:
Add CPU and GPU backend support for HloOpcode::kFma

Lower `fma` (strict single-rounded IEEE-754 fused multiply-add) across XLA CPU

display_title: Ignore element size and memory space in CommonPjRtClient::Delinearize.

head_commit.message:
Ignore element size and memory space in CommonPjRtClient::Delinearize.

XLA `Literal` shapes always clear `element_size_in_bits` to 0 (storing sub-byte elements unpacked at 1 byte per element) and use the default `memory_space`, whereas PJRT buffer shapes carry packed `element_size_in_bits` (for example, 4 for `S4`/`U4` or 2 for `S2`/`U2`) and the buffer's `memory_space` (such as `Layout::kHostMemorySpace`). Comparing `literal_layout != shape.layout()` in `CommonPjRtClient::Delinearize` therefore always evaluated `need_transpose = true` for every sub-byte buffer and every host-memory-space buffer, even when the rest of the layout already matched. For sub-byte transfers, that forced an unnecessary heap allocation and zero-fill of `staged_buffer` at the full unpacked byte size followed by an identity `TransposePlan::Execute` copy on top of `UnpackIntN`, leaving the direct `UnpackIntN` branch unreachable.

Compare layouts in `CommonPjRtClient::Delinearize` with `Layout::Equal().IgnoreElementSize().IgnoreMemorySpace()`, taking the direct unpack or `memcpy` fast path when layouts otherwise match (and guarding `std::memcpy` on 0-byte outputs). On `BM_DelinearizeInt4`, this speeds up `S4` delinearization by 3.1x–3.7x for cache-resident buffers (4 Ki and 1 Mi elements, reaching 31–37 GiB/s) and by 9.7x for 64 Mi-element buffers (48.1 ms to 4.95 ms) by avoiding transient 64 MiB `staged_buffer` page faults and copies.

Tested with unit tests in `//xla/pjrt:common_pjrt_client_test` covering matching default and non-default `minor_to_major` sub-byte layouts, odd-element tail-byte masking, transposed sub-byte layouts, `kHostMemorySpace` buffers (including 0-element spans), and end-to-end `BufferFromHostLiteral` to `ToLiteral` round-trips, alongside `BM_DelinearizeInt4` microbenchmarks.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Use typed LiteralUtil::CreateR0<T> in HandleAllReduceOrReduceScatter.

In `AlgebraicSimplifierVisitor::HandleAllReduceOrReduceScatter` (`xla/hlo/transforms/simplifiers/algebraic_simplifier.cc`), the `ReductionKind::SUM` constant-folding branch is already inside a `primitive_util::ArrayTypeSwitch` over `element_type` where `using T = primitive_util::NativeTypeOf<type_constant>` is the native C++ type corresponding to `element_type`. Calling the 2-argument `LiteralUtil::CreateR0(element_type, result)` instead of the 1-argument `LiteralUtil::CreateR0<T>(result)` caused `CreateR0(PrimitiveType, T)` to instantiate a nested 29-way `ArrayTypeSwitch` for each of the 27 integral and floating-point types `T` (`27 × 29 = 783` cross-type `static_cast<NativeT>(result)` branches), adding 151.6 KB to `algebraic_simplifier.pic.o`.

Call `LiteralUtil::CreateR0<T>(result)` directly, matching `MakeScalarInstruction` in the same file.

Runtime and memory performance impact: Zero memory overhead and slightly faster constant folding for `AllReduce`/`ReduceScatter` of a scalar constant by avoiding a redundant runtime `ArrayTypeSwitch` dispatch.

display_title: Optimize `xla::BackendConfigWrapper::empty` by caching emptiness in `bool empty_`.

head_commit.message:
Optimize `xla::BackendConfigWrapper::empty` by caching emptiness in `bool empty_`.

`xla::BackendConfigWrapper::empty()` (called by `HloInstruction::has_backend_config()`) previously acquired `absl::MutexLock lock(mutex_)` on every call just to check `proto_ == nullptr && raw_string_.empty()`. When multiple threads concurrently query `has_backend_config()` on shared HLO instructions, they heavily contend on `BackendConfigWrapper::mutex_`.

This change:
- Tracks whether `BackendConfigWrapper` is empty in a `bool empty_ = true;` member updated on construction and move-assignment, allowing `empty()` to read `empty_` without locking `mutex_`.
- Adds fast paths to `BackendConfigWrapper::operator==` (`this == &other` and `empty() && other.empty()`) to avoid mutex acquisition and string formatting when comparing empty configs.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add ScanRewriterTriton to the GPU compiler pipeline behind a flag.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add ScanRewriterTriton to the GPU compiler pipeline behind a flag.

Add the debug option `xla_gpu_experimental_enable_triton_scan` (default off). When it is set, `GpuCompiler` runs `ScanRewriterTriton` in `OptimizeHloPostLayoutAssignment` before `AssociativeScanRewriter`, so eligible associative `kScan` instructions become Triton scan fusions instead of reduce-window trees.

The rewriter only sets the fusion kind to `__triton`; the tiling is chosen later by `PriorityFusion`, `FusionBlockLevelRewriter` or the autotuner.

`GpuCompiler` only adds the rewriter on GPUs that Triton supports. A tiled scan computes one row per block, so scans with a dimension of at least 32768 also need at least 64 rows (`kMinRowsForLongScan`); otherwise the hierarchical scan of `AssociativeScanRewriter` is faster (crossover at 64 rows on H100 and 32 on B200). Shorter scans are faster with Triton at any batch size.

`CanTritonHandleScan` now rejects scans over any dimension other than the last one, for which the tiled Triton scan computes wrong results.

For a cumsum with an elementwise epilogue on f32[B, N], with B from 1 to 256 and N from 1024 to 262144, enabling the flag is never slower on H100 and B200. It is 1.05–2.9x (H100) and 1.06–2.8x (B200) faster for N < 32768, and up to 1.9x (H100) and 2.3x (B200) faster for N ≥ 32768 and B ≥ 64.

A top-p sampling mask (softmax, cumsum, compare and select) on f32[B, K] with B from 1 to 256 and K in {64, 128} compiles to a single Triton kernel: 1.3–1.5 µs instead of 3.3–4.5 µs on H100, and 2.5–3.1 µs instead of 5.9–8.4 µs on B200.

head_commit.message:
Deduplicate op-independent conversion helpers in `hlo_legalize_to_stablehlo`.

`HloToStablehloOpConverter<StablehloOpTy>` and `HloToStablehloCustomCallOpConverter<HloOpTy>` instantiate conversion patterns across all ~135 StableHLO and MHLO operations in `xla/mlir_hlo/mhlo/transforms/hlo_legalize_to_stablehlo/hlo_legalize_to_stablehlo.cc`. Previously, `convertAttributes`, `isDenseI64Array`, `convertDenseArray`, and `rewriteMhloOpAsCustomCall` were templated on `HloOpTy` / `StablehloOpTy` without `if constexpr`, causing `convertAttributes` and the region-inlining loop to be emitted separately for every op (and requiring an explicit 11-op `if constexpr` exclusion list in `convertAttributes` for MHLO-only ops without a `HloToStablehloOp` mapping). In addition, `hasPrivateFeaturesNotInStablehlo<HloOpTy>` checked the 10 XLA-private op types via runtime `isa<...>` in every pattern instantiation rather than compile-time `if constexpr`.

Make `isDenseI64Array`, `convertDenseArray`, `convertAttributes`, `convertTypesAndAttributes`, `convertRegions`, and `rewriteMhloOpAsCustomCall` non-template helpers operating on `Operation*`, check `hasPrivateFeaturesNotInStablehlo<HloOpTy>` at compile time with `if constexpr (llvm::is_one_of<HloOpTy, ...>::value)`, and guard `convertRegions` with `if constexpr (!HloOpTy::template hasTrait<OpTrait::ZeroRegions>())`. In addition, hoist `dyn_cast<mhlo::CustomCallOp>(hloOp)` out of the attribute loop in `convertAttributes`, mutate `NamedAttribute` values in place (`hloAttr.setValue(stablehloAttr)`), fetch `hloAttr.getName().getValue()` only after `dyn_cast<DenseIntElementsAttr>` succeeds in `convertDenseArray`, and pass `getPublicFeaturesNotInStablehlo(hloOp)` into `rewriteMhloOpAsCustomCall` instead of recomputing it.

Runtime and memory performance impact: Zero memory overhead (`+0.00%` allocations and peak memory) and `-2.23%` faster geomean CPU time (`-2.24%` wall time) across 8 `createHloLegalizeToStablehloPass` microbenchmarks.

head_commit.message:
Implement `Client::CancelExecution` in IFRT Proxy.

`xla::ifrt::proxy::Client::CancelExecution` was previously a no-op stub, which prevented client-side execution cancellation (such as MPMD reshard cancellation) from propagating through IFRT Proxy to the server backend.

Bump the IFRT Proxy protocol version to `kCancelExecution` (26), add `cancellation_handle` to `LoadedExecutableExecuteRequest`, and introduce `CancelExecutionRequest` and `CancelExecutionResponse` in `ifrt_service.proto`. On the client, `LoadedExecutable::Execute` mints a `cancellation_handle` and returns a `ProxyCancellationHandle` wrapping it, and `Client::CancelExecution` sends `CancelExecutionRequest` to the server. On the server, `IfrtBackend` stores the underlying `CancellationHandle` from `LoadedExecutable::Execute` until the execution completes, is cancelled via `HandleCancelExecutionRequest`, or the executable is destroyed.

In-flight executions dispatched through `xla::ifrt::proxy::Client` can now be cancelled via `Client::CancelExecution`, with unit tests covering the client, executable, and backend handlers.

display_title: [XLA] Deduplicate HloEvaluator unary op setup and dead handlers.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Deduplicate HloEvaluator unary op setup and dead handlers.

`HloEvaluatorTypedVisitor<ReturnT, ElementwiseT>` is instantiated across 32 primitive types, duplicating shape/layout validation, operand `Literal` lookup, result `Literal` allocation, and `absl::StatusOr<Literal>` move/teardown across unary `Handle*` instantiations, while also instantiating 26 floating-point/complex unary handlers on `bool` and 14 integer types via C++11 `<cmath>` integral overloads (`double std::sin(Integral)`, etc.) that upstream `ShapeInference::InferUnaryOpShape` / `HloVerifier` already reject.

```
// Before (duplicated per type T and per unary Handle* opcode):
HandleOp(hlo): ASSIGN_OR_RETURN(Literal lit, ElementWiseUnaryOp(hlo, fn));
               parent_->SetEvaluatedLiteralFor(hlo, std::move(lit));

// After (shared non-template setup/storage; typed inner loop captured by value):
HandleOp(hlo): if constexpr (valid_for_ElementwiseT)  // for 26 FP/complex ops
                 return ElementWiseUnaryOp(hlo, fn);  // -> RunElementwiseUnaryOp(...)
```

Specifically:
- Factor type-independent shape checks, operand lookup, `Literal(shape)` allocation, and `SetEvaluatedLiteralFor` storage into non-template `HloEvaluator::RunElementwiseUnaryOp` in `xla/hlo/evaluator/hlo_evaluator.cc`, returning `absl::Status` directly from `ElementWiseUnaryOp` / `ElementWiseUnaryOpImpl`.
- Capture `operand_data` and `unary_op` (`absl::FunctionRef`) by value in `ElementWiseUnaryOpImpl`'s `PopulateLinearParallel` / `PopulateParallel` lambdas instead of wrapping via `ConvertUnaryFunction`'s `[&]` lambda, eliminating 3 pointer-chasing memory loads per element inside `MutableLiteralBase::PopulateLinearInplaceInternal`'s type-erased `FunctionRef` callback.
- Guard the 26 floating-point and floating-or-complex unary handlers (`HandleSin`, `HandleCos`, `HandleExp`, `HandleRound`, `HandleFloor`, `HandleCeil`, etc.) with `if constexpr` on `ElementwiseT` matching `ShapeInference::InferUnaryOpShape`, avoiding dead elementwise loop instantiations across the 15 `PRED`/integral visitors and returning `UnsupportedTypeError` if an unverified instruction reaches `HloEvaluator`.

**Runtime & Memory Performance Impact:**
- **CPU:** Improves `BM_UnaryOp/512` by 6.97% and `BM_UnaryOp/1024` by 6.68% (`p=0.000`, 20-run `-c opt --config=benchmark`) in `//xla/hlo/evaluator:hlo_evaluator_test`, because storing `operand_data` and `unary_op` inline in the `PopulateLinearParallel` lambda removes 3 pointer-dereference loads per element across the per-element indirect callback (`18 -> 15` instructions/element for `F32` `exp`).
- **Memory:** Heap allocations are unchanged (`Literal(shape)` is allocated once and moved directly into `EvaluationState`), and per-op stack usage drops from 768 B to 32 B in `ElementWiseUnaryOpImpl` by removing intermediate `absl::StatusOr<Literal>` stack frames.

display_title: [XLA] Deduplicate HloEvaluator binary and ternary elementwise setup.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Deduplicate HloEvaluator binary and ternary elementwise setup.

`HloEvaluatorTypedVisitor<ReturnT, ElementwiseT>` is instantiated across 32 primitive types, duplicating shape/layout validation, operand `Literal` lookup, result `Literal` allocation, and `absl::StatusOr<Literal>` move/teardown across binary and ternary `Handle*` instantiations.

```
// Before (duplicated per type T and per binary/ternary Handle* opcode):
HandleOp(hlo): ASSIGN_OR_RETURN(Literal lit, ElementWiseBinaryOp(hlo, fn));
               parent_->SetEvaluatedLiteralFor(hlo, std::move(lit));

// After (shared non-template setup/storage; typed inner loop captured by value):
HandleOp(hlo): return ElementWiseBinaryOp(hlo, fn);  // -> RunElementwiseBinaryOp(...)
```

Specifically:
- Factor type-independent shape/scalar checks, operand lookup, `Literal(shape)` allocation, and `SetEvaluatedLiteralFor` storage into non-template `HloEvaluator::RunElementwiseBinaryOp` and `HloEvaluator::RunElementwiseTernaryOp` helpers in `xla/hlo/evaluator/hlo_evaluator.cc`, returning `absl::Status` directly and dropping redundant `<ReturnT, ReturnT, ReturnT>` template parameters on `ElementwiseTernaryOp`.
- Capture raw operand data pointers, scalar flags, and `absl::FunctionRef`s by value in `ElementWiseBinaryOpImpl` and `ElementwiseTernaryOpImpl`'s `PopulateLinearParallel` / `PopulateParallel` lambdas (instead of `[&]` captures and `ConvertBinaryFunction`'s `[&]` wrapper), eliminating 3 pointer-chasing memory loads per element inside `MutableLiteralBase::PopulateLinearInplaceInternal`'s type-erased `FunctionRef` callback.

**Runtime & Memory Performance Impact:**
- **CPU:** Improves `BM_BinaryOp/512` by 7.74% and `BM_BinaryOp/1024` by 9.68% (`p=0.000`, 20-run `-c opt --config=benchmark`) in `//xla/hlo/evaluator:hlo_evaluator_test`, because storing `lhs_data`, `rhs_data`, and `binary_op` inline in the `PopulateLinearParallel` lambda removes 3 pointer-dereference loads per element across the per-element indirect callback (`20 -> 17` instructions/element for `F32` `add`).
- **Memory:** Heap allocations are unchanged (`Literal(shape)` is allocated once and moved directly into `EvaluationState`), and per-op stack usage shrinks by removing intermediate `absl::StatusOr<Literal>` return frames.

display_title: [XLA] Deduplicate HloEvaluator unary op setup and dead handlers.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Deduplicate HloEvaluator elementwise setup and dead unary handlers

`HloEvaluatorTypedVisitor<ReturnT, ElementwiseT>` is instantiated across 32 primitive types, duplicating shape/layout validation, operand `Literal` lookup, result `Literal` allocation, and `absl::StatusOr<Literal>` move/teardown across ~1,200 `Handle*` instantiations, while also instantiating 26 floating-point/complex unary handlers on `bool` and 14 integer types via `<cmath>` integral overloads rejected by `ShapeInference::InferUnaryOpShape`.

```
// Before (duplicated per type T and per Handle* opcode):
HandleOp(hlo): ASSIGN_OR_RETURN(Literal lit, ElementWise*Op(hlo, fn));
               parent_->SetEvaluatedLiteralFor(hlo, std::move(lit));

// After (shared non-template setup/storage; typed inner loop inlined by value):
HandleOp(hlo): if constexpr (valid_for_ElementwiseT)  // for 26 FP/complex ops
                 return ElementWise*Op(hlo, fn);      // -> RunElementwise*Op(...)
```

Specifically:
- Factor type-independent shape checks, operand lookup, `Literal(shape)` allocation, and `SetEvaluatedLiteralFor` storage into non-template `HloEvaluator::RunElementwise{Unary,Binary,Ternary}Op` helpers in `xla/hlo/evaluator/hlo_evaluator.cc`, returning `absl::Status` directly and dropping unused template parameters on `ElementwiseTernaryOp`.
- Capture raw operand/output data pointers and `absl::FunctionRef`s by value in `PopulateLinearParallel` / `PopulateParallel` worker lambdas to avoid cross-stack-frame reference indirection while keeping the inner per-element loops fully typed and inline.
- Guard the 26 floating-point and floating-or-complex unary handlers (`HandleSin`, `HandleCos`, `HandleExp`, `HandleRound`, `HandleFloor`, `HandleCeil`, etc.) with `if constexpr` on `ElementwiseT` matching `ShapeInference::InferUnaryOpShape`.

**Runtime & Memory Performance Impact:**
- **CPU:** Geomean CPU time improves by 7.52% across `BM_UnaryOp` and `BM_BinaryOp` in `//xla/hlo/evaluator:hlo_evaluator_test` (`-7.05%` on `BM_UnaryOp/1024`, `-13.48%` on `BM_BinaryOp/1024`), as typed inner loops capture raw buffer pointers by value on worker threads and returning `absl::Status` eliminates two `Literal` moves and destructors per op.
- **Memory:** Heap allocations are unchanged (`Literal(shape)` is allocated once and moved directly into `EvaluationState`), and per-op stack usage drops by ~1 KB by removing intermediate `absl::StatusOr<Literal>` stack frames.

head_commit.message:
[IFRT] Canonicalize names in MLIR fingerprints

`FingerprintModuleOp` hashes the module name and the symbol names of `sdy.mesh`
ops, so programs that differ only in these names get different fingerprints.
`FingerprintOptions` adds `canonicalize_module_name` and
`canonicalize_sdy_mesh_names`, which a bytecode attribute callback implements by
encoding these names as IDs. Mesh definitions, mesh uses and the order of mesh
names still contribute, and the IR is not mutated. `FingerprintModuleOp` and
`HloProgram::Fingerprint` take the options explicitly; default options keep
existing fingerprints.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1004481564

head_commit.message:
[PJRT] Restore --xla_dump_hlo_snapshots for single-device GPU executions

Optimized-module HLO snapshot dumping was lost on GPU when execution moved
off LocalExecutable::RunAsync onto the direct GpuExecutable::ExecuteThunks
path. The CPU client kept its own dump, which now lives in the CPU-only
fast path of CommonPjRtLoadedExecutable::Execute; clients that take the
general path (StreamExecutor GPU among them) never dump.

Dump the snapshot in the general single-device path as well: once before
the run (crash-safe, without results) and once after with the result
literals, using the same MaybeDumpHloSnapshot helper and file name as the
CPU path. Executables that do not expose an HloModule are skipped.

Adds a GPU regression test mirroring PjRtCpuClientTest.HloSnapshot.

Fixes #39194.

display_title: [IFRT IR] Serialize IfrtIrLoadedExecutable memory tracer queries.

head_commit.message:
[IFRT IR] Serialize IfrtIrLoadedExecutable memory tracer queries.

`GetIfrtIrProgramMemoryStats()` and `GetIfrtIrProgramXprofUrl()` are const
methods, but both call into `ProgramMemoryTracer`, which builds and caches its
memory trace on first use without synchronization. Concurrent first calls race
on the cached trace and on the maps used to build it. Guard the tracer with a
mutex in `IfrtIrLoadedExecutable`, like `delete_options_`.

Adds a test that queries the memory stats from several threads.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1006338542
